newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei stock index rises 2 pct as yen falls.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei stock index rises 2 pct as yen falls.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's key index surged by two percent in mid-afternoon trade on Thursday, as the yen's sharp fall against the dollar after remarks by an influential Finance Ministry official spurred buying of leading Japanese exporters, brokers said.
At 0448 GMT, the 225-share Nikkei average was up 366.04 points, or 1.80 percent, to trade at 20,655.97, after briefly rising by two percent.
June Nikkei futures were 350 points higher at 20,660.
The dollar briefly shot up above 115.00 yen, after senior Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara said Japan will act decisively against excessive forex moves.
Sakakibara, who attended a financial seminar on Thursday, was also quoted as saying that Japan's trade surplus will not be a major issue at the Group of Seven (G7) summit meeting later this month.
